title: Supply Chain & Logistics
tagline: Plan, source, make, and deliver — master the flow of goods that keeps every business running.
summary: Supply chain professionals coordinate forecasting, procurement, production, inventory, warehousing, and transportation so products arrive where they're needed at the lowest total cost. This roadmap follows the end-to-end flow — plan, source, make, deliver — and the certifications (CPIM, CSCP, CLTD, Six Sigma) that anchor the profession.

detail.description: Supply chain management coordinates everything between raw material and customer: planning, sourcing, manufacturing, inventory, warehousing, and delivery. The classic frame is plan–source–make–deliver–return.
detail.why: Pandemic-era shortages made supply chain strategy visible to every board. It is a large, stable profession with clear certifications and strong demand for planners and analysts.
learn: Read the BLS profile of logisticians
Draw the SCOR-style flow: plan, source, make, deliver, return
Trace one product you own backward through its chain
Identify 3 industries whose supply chains differ fundamentally (grocery vs aerospace vs fashion)
tasks: Analyze and coordinate the logistical functions of an organization, including movement of materials, information, and products.

detail.description: Every chain is a set of linked decisions: how much to make (plan), from whom to buy (source), how to produce (make), and how to ship (deliver). Each link holds inventory and adds lead time.
detail.why: Seeing the whole flow lets you find where cost and delay actually accumulate — the core diagnostic skill of the profession.
learn: Map one company's chain from supplier's supplier to customer's customer
Define upstream vs downstream and first-tier vs second-tier suppliers
Explain the bullwhip effect with a simple example
Identify the two biggest lead-time contributors in your map

resources.title: ASCM — Supply chain body of knowledge

detail.description: Planning runs on spreadsheets: forecasts, order schedules, inventory projections, and vendor scorecards. Lookup functions, pivot tables, and clean data discipline are daily tools.
detail.why: Supply chain roles interview with Excel cases. Fluency here is the fastest way to contribute in your first planning job.
learn: Build a reorder-point calculator with formulas
Summarize 12 months of demand with PivotTables
Use XLOOKUP to join a price list to an order file
Practice clean-data habits: dates, units, one fact per cell

detail.description: Chains differ by industry: grocery optimizes freshness and speed, aerospace optimizes traceability and downtime cost, fashion optimizes trend timing, pharma adds regulatory custody requirements.
detail.why: Your industry choice shapes your whole career — pick deliberately after seeing how the problems differ.
learn: Compare inventory logic in grocery vs aerospace
Learn what makes pharma chains special (batch traceability, cold chain)
Note the manufacturing vs retail vs 3PL employer split
Pick two domains to read industry news about for a month

detail.description: Forecasting estimates future demand using history and market signals: moving averages, seasonality, trend, and forecast error measures like MAPE and bias.
detail.why: Every downstream decision — buying, staffing, shipping — inherits the forecast's error. Planners live and die by forecast quality.
learn: Compute a 3-month moving average forecast
Detect seasonality in 24 months of demand data
Measure error with MAPE and track bias
Explain why consensus forecasts beat single-source guesses
tasks: Plan, direct, or coordinate the work of employees and workers engaged in production or logistics.

detail.description: Sales & operations planning is the monthly executive process that balances demand, supply, and money into one operating plan: data review, demand plan, supply plan, reconciliation, executive sign-off.
detail.why: S&OP is where supply chain meets the C-suite. Understanding it marks you as management-track rather than execution-track.
learn: Diagram the 5-step monthly S&OP cycle
Identify the trade-offs each step reconciles (service vs inventory vs cost)
Simulate one cycle with sample data in a spreadsheet
Write the one-page agenda an S&OP chair would use

resources.title: ASCM — Supply chain body of knowledge

detail.description: Capacity planning matches demand to available resources — machines, lines, people, warehouse space — across rough-cut and detailed time horizons, deciding when to add, outsource, or level-load.
detail.why: Capacity decisions lock in costs for years. Planners who can model them credibly become indispensable.
learn: Compute utilization and efficiency for one resource
Run a rough-cut capacity plan against a demand plan
Compare overtime, outsourcing, and capex responses to a 20% demand spike
Explain the cost of capacity decisions made too late

resources.title: O*NET — Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks

detail.description: Procurement turns requirements into supply: needs specification, supplier identification, RFQ/RFP, evaluation, negotiation, purchase orders, receipt, and payment — the source-to-pay cycle.
detail.why: Purchased goods are often the largest cost line; procurement skills pay directly and procurement is a career path of its own.
learn: Map the source-to-pay cycle end to end
Write a one-page RFQ for a simple category
Score two suppliers on cost, quality, delivery, risk
Understand 3-way match: PO, receipt, invoice
tasks: Purchase raw or semifinished materials, machinery, or equipment for an organization; evaluate suppliers and negotiate contracts.

detail.description: Choosing suppliers balances price against quality, delivery reliability, capacity, financial health, and risk — then manages the relationship with scorecards and regular reviews.
detail.why: A bad supplier quietly taxes every downstream step. Supplier management is where procurement adds value beyond buying cheap.
learn: Build a weighted supplier scorecard (cost, quality, delivery, risk)
Run a mock supplier audit checklist
Design a quarterly business review agenda
Plan dual sourcing for a critical component

resources.title: ASCM — Supply chain body of knowledge

detail.description: Purchase orders and supply agreements fix quantity, price, lead time, quality terms, and remedies. Key structures include blanket POs, scheduling agreements, and Incoterms-based shipping responsibilities.
detail.why: When things go wrong, the contract is the recovery path. Reading a supply agreement without fear is a professional superpower.
learn: Identify the essential terms of a PO
Compare spot buys vs blanket orders vs long-term agreements
Read a sample clause set: liability, lead time, price adjustment
Escalate a late-delivery scenario using contract terms

detail.description: Production planning schedules what gets made when: master scheduling, MRP logic (what, how many, when, given lead times and inventory), lot sizing, and priority management.
detail.why: This is the operational heart of manufacturing supply chains and the daily work of planning clerks and production planners.
learn: Run MRP logic by hand on a 2-level product tree
Build a weekly master schedule with rough-cut capacity check
Compare push (MRP) vs pull (kanban) scheduling
Expedite and de-expedite: how planners re-prioritize honestly

detail.description: Lean targets the classic seven wastes (overproduction, waiting, transport, overprocessing, inventory, motion, defects) with tools like 5S, kanban pull, standard work, and kaizen events.
detail.why: Lean vocabulary dominates operations job interviews, and lean thinking improves every process you'll ever touch.
learn: Name the 7 wastes with a supply chain example each
Run a personal 5S on your workspace and time the effect
Explain how kanban limits work-in-progress
Draft a kaizen proposal: problem, root cause, countermeasure, result measure

detail.description: Quality management keeps output within specification: inspection, statistical process control, root-cause analysis, and the Six Sigma DMAIC improvement cycle (define, measure, analyze, improve, control).
detail.why: Quality failures ripple down entire chains. Six Sigma belts are widely recognized credentials for operations careers.
learn: Explain DMAIC and what happens at each phase
Run a basic root-cause session (5 whys + fishbone)
Read a control chart: common vs special cause variation
Compute a defect rate and convert it to Sigma level roughly

detail.description: Inventory management balances service against cost: ABC classification, cycle counting, turnover targets, and the trade-off between stockouts and carrying cost.
detail.why: Inventory is where working capital hides. Planners who can explain and manage it are among the most valued roles in retail and manufacturing.
learn: ABC-classify 50 SKUs by value contribution
Compute inventory turns and days of supply
Explain the cost of overstock vs stockout for one product
Design a cycle-counting program with tolerances

detail.description: Safety stock buffers demand and supply variability; reorder points and order quantities (EOQ logic) decide when and how much to buy. Service-level targets set the buffer math.
detail.why: This is the bread-and-butter calculation of planning roles and a guaranteed CPIM exam topic.
learn: Compute a reorder point from demand and lead time
Calculate safety stock from service level and variability (basic z-score method)
Explain EOQ and its real-world caveats
Tune buffers after a stockout without overshooting

detail.description: Warehouse operations flow through receiving, putaway, storage, picking, packing, and shipping — measured in accuracy, throughput, and cost per unit handled.
detail.why: Distribution centers are major employers and the proving ground for many operations leaders; understanding them helps every planner.
learn: Map the 6 warehouse process steps
Compare piece, batch, and zone picking and when each wins
Compute order accuracy and lines-per-hour
Slot 20 SKUs by velocity (ABC slotting)

resources.title: O*NET — Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers

detail.description: Transportation moves freight across modes — parcel, LTL, FTL, rail, ocean, air — trading speed against cost, with routing, carrier selection, and freight terms governing the details.
detail.why: Freight is often a top-three cost line. Transportation knowledge spans daily ops work and network design roles alike.
learn: Compare 5 modes on speed, cost, and use cases
Explain parcel vs LTL vs FTL with rate examples
Read a basic freight quote: accessorials, fuel, terms
Plan a cost-mode trade-off for a 2-day vs 7-day promise

resources.title: O*NET — Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers

tasks: Direct transportation, distribution, and storage activities in accordance with organizational policies and applicable government laws or regulations.

detail.description: Incoterms are the ICC's standardized three-letter terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP and others) defining who pays for and risks each leg of an international shipment.
detail.why: Cross-border buying and selling run on Incoterms; misreading one term can shift thousands in freight cost and risk to the wrong party.
learn: Learn the 11 current Incoterms and group them by transport mode
Explain who arranges carriage and insurance under FOB vs CIF vs DDP
Trace cost/risk transfer points on a shipment timeline
Pick the right term for a sample import scenario

resources.title: International Chamber of Commerce — Incoterms rules

detail.description: Supply chains run on systems: ERP (SAP, Oracle, Dynamics) for planning and transactions, WMS for warehouse execution, TMS for freight, and EDI for system-to-system documents like POs and ASNs.
detail.why: Every planning role touches these systems; data and implementation skills (key user, super user) are a well-paid specialization.
learn: Map which master data lives where (item, BOM, vendor, customer)
Trace an order through ERP → WMS → carrier → invoice
Explain what EDI documents 850, 856, 810 do
Practice as a 'key user': write one test script for a system change

detail.description: The scoreboard: OTIF (on-time-in-full), fill rate, forecast accuracy, inventory turns, days of supply, perfect order rate, cost-to-serve, and cash-to-cash cycle time.
detail.why: KPIs structure every review meeting. Choosing and defending the right ones is how analysts get promoted.
learn: Define and compute OTIF, fill rate, and turns
Build a one-page KPI dashboard from sample data
Explain the service-vs-inventory tension behind two KPIs
Propose one corrective action for a failing KPI

resources.title: ASCM — Supply chain body of knowledge

detail.description: Resilience planning anticipates disruption: supplier risk scoring, dual sourcing, strategic buffers, nearshoring, and playbooks for port closures, shortages, and demand shocks.
detail.why: Post-pandemic, resilience budgets are real. Engineers of resilience — planners who price the buffer — have become strategic hires.
learn: Score 5 suppliers on single-source and geopolitical risk
Price the trade-off: buffer inventory vs expedite freight vs lost sales
Write a disruption playbook for one scenario
Explain how nearshoring changes total landed cost

resources.title: ASCM — Supply chain body of knowledge

detail.description: Green supply chain reduces freight emissions, packaging, and waste: mode shifting, load consolidation, reusable packaging, circular flows, and ESG reporting basics.
detail.why: Regulation and customer pressure are pushing sustainability into every freight and sourcing decision — an emerging specialty with room to lead.
learn: Estimate the emissions difference between air and ocean for one shipment
List 5 packaging waste reductions with cost impact
Understand Scope 1/2/3 emissions at a high level
Draft a greener-routing proposal with trade-offs

resources.title: ASCM — Supply chain body of knowledge

detail.description: Modern retail fulfills from everywhere: stores as mini-DCs, ship-from-store, buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPIS), and marketplace returns — each adding planning and reverse-logistics complexity.
detail.why: Retail supply chain jobs are numerous and growing; omnichannel literacy is required in nearly all of them.
learn: Compare fulfillment economics: ship-from-DC vs ship-from-store vs BOPIS
Explain reverse logistics and its cost drivers
Design returns handling for an online apparel brand
Plan labor for a Black Friday BOPIS surge

detail.description: Typical ladder: analyst/coordinator → planner or logistics specialist → manager (planning, transportation, warehouse) → director of supply chain → VP/CSCO. Procurement and consulting are strong lateral tracks.
detail.why: Supply chain leadership is increasingly a board-visible career. Knowing the ladder shapes which certification and which first job to target.
learn: Scan 20 postings in your market and cluster the titles
Choose a first anchor: planning, logistics, or procurement
Map which certification each track values most
Draft a 5-year goal and the two roles bridging to it

resources.title: O*NET — Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers

detail.description: The Certified in Planning and Inventory Management credential (ASCM, formerly APICS) is the standard for production planning, forecasting, and inventory roles — two exam modules covering the planning body of knowledge.
detail.why: CPIM is the most requested certification for planner and production-control jobs; it directly teaches the daily math of the role.
learn: Review CPIM exam structure and topic weights
Study through ASCM's official learning system
Practice MRP, safety stock, and EOQ problems until fluent
Check your local job postings: how often is CPIM listed?

certs.name: CPIM
certs.note: Pass the two-part CPIM exam (learning modules plus exam preparation); credential requires ongoing maintenance points.

detail.description: The Certified Supply Chain Professional (ASCM) covers the full end-to-end chain — supplier relationships through customer delivery — at a broader, more strategic level than CPIM.
detail.why: CSCP suits people targeting network-level roles, consulting, or management; it signals whole-chain literacy.
learn: Compare CSCP scope with CPIM scope
Review eligibility: degree and/or experience requirements
Study the technology and integration sections carefully (heavily tested)
Decide CPIM-first vs CSCP-first based on your anchor role

certs.name: CSCP
certs.note: Meet the eligibility rule (degree and/or years of professional experience), pass the exam; maintenance points required.

detail.description: The Certified in Logistics, Transportation and Distribution (ASCM) credential specializes in warehouse, freight, and distribution knowledge — the operational side of the chain.
detail.why: CLTD is the recognized credential for DC management and transportation careers, complementing planning-focused CPIM.
learn: Review CLTD domains: logistics strategy, warehouse, transport, distribution
Pair study with DC floor exposure if possible
Compare CLTD vs CPIM for your target track
Check exam logistics and maintenance requirements

certs.name: CLTD
certs.note: Pass the CLTD exam covering logistics, transportation, and distribution; maintenance points required.

detail.description: ASQ's Certified Six Sigma Green Belt (and Yellow/Black Belt) credentials validate the DMAIC improvement method, statistics, and process control — widely respected in operations and quality roles.
detail.why: A Green Belt with a real project story is one of the strongest differentiators for early-career operations and continuous-improvement roles.
learn: Take ASQ's free Yellow Belt body-of-knowledge overview
Complete one small DMAIC project at work or on simulated data
Learn the core statistics: variation, capability, sampling
Decide Green Belt vs Black Belt timing

certs.name: Six Sigma Green Belt
certs.note: Pass the exam; Green Belt certification expects familiarity with DMAIC projects (ASQ requires work experience for several quality credentials — check current rules).

detail.description: Entry doors include demand planner, inventory analyst, logistics coordinator, buyer assistant, and production scheduler. They reward Excel, reliability, and calm communication under expediting pressure.
detail.why: Breaking in is about proof: a portfolio of small analyses (stockout post-mortem, freight comparison, forecast accuracy tracker) beats generic resumes.
learn: Build 3 portfolio artifacts: forecast tracker, freight cost comparison, KPI one-pager
Practice the classic interview case: 'demand doubled, what do you do?'
Learn to talk expediting without panic in interviews
Target distributors, 3PLs, and mid-size manufacturers — highest entry volume
